claims.text: Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers provide adequate mechanical strength.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have suboptimal heat dissipation.
Controlled directional solidification will promote an aligned dual-phase microstructure.
Controlled directional solidification will produce an interconnected, high-electron-conductivity phase embedded in the matrix.
The matrix and high-conductivity phase will have coherent interfaces.
Directional solidification will align a high-thermal-conductivity phase into a continuous network.
The continuous high-thermal-conductivity network will channel heat more efficiently.
The remaining matrix will maintain structural strength through retained, well-bonded microstructural features.
The directionally solidified alloy will have higher thermal conductivity than conventionally processed intermediate-layer high-entropy alloys.
The thermal-conductivity improvement will occur without compromising mechanical integrity.
Conventionally processed intermediate-layer high-entropy alloys have good structural integrity.
Conventionally processed intermediate-layer high-entropy alloys have limited heat-transfer efficiency.
The proposed effect should persist under the operational temperatures and mechanical loads typical of plasma-facing reactor components.
